transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Laila Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Marisa Gomez (Crestline VP Infra), Ethan Park (Head AI), Priya Singh (Security), Tom Hsu (SRE)

Summary: quick check-in on renewal and expansion: discussing Dedicated capacity increase, adding EU and AP regions, and compliance gating items. Decision leaning Dedicated but security needs docs. Agreed to run benchmarks in eu-west.

00:00:00 - Laila Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro, i'm laila from Redwood, this is ravi our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:00:12 - Marisa Gomez: good, thanks. we'll keep this tight, a few execs are in back-to-back.
00:00:20 - Ravi Patel: great, agenda is renewal timeline, capacity upgrade, regions, security asks, and then next steps.
00:00:34 - Ethan Park: sounds good. we sent our traffic profile earlier, tom will chime in on SRE constraints.
00:00:42 - Tom Hsu: yep, i'll walk the expected rps and seq len.
00:00:50 - Laila Chen: quick status check: i saw usage up about 2.6x QoQ, and the current hosted tier is hitting some p99 spikes, right? just to confirm.
00:01:03 - Ethan Park: yeah, p99 spikes during batch jobs and at end of day. we're looking at dedicated to get predictable throughput and to expand to eu and ap for latency to customers.
00:01:18 - Laila Chen: perfect. marisa, what's the preferred renewal window? are we looking to sign an extension before year-end?
00:01:27 - Marisa Gomez: yes, procurement wants a decision by end of October. ideally we pick a 12 or 24 month commit depending on pricing.
00:01:36 - Laila Chen: understood. ravi, can you recap the 6-node dedicated plan we proposed?
00:01:42 - Ravi Patel: sure — the 6-node Dedicated pool gives you reserved GPU capacity, autoscale policies for burst, and we can tune batching and prefix caching. for the models you're running we'd expect linear throughput increases and lower tail latency. note that quantization profiles we recommend (int8-ish) reduce cost but we still keep KV cache to avoid regen costs.
00:02:05 - Priya Singh: quick security question — does Dedicated mean customer data leaves region? we need local residency for eu-west.
00:02:14 - Ravi Patel: good question. for Dedicated hosted in eu-west the data is processed in-region and logs can be routed to your KMS; we also support customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). for full on-prem Private, the control plane can be customer-managed but that adds integration time.
00:02:31 - Priya Singh: can you send the KMS integration doc and SOC2 report?
00:02:36 - Laila Chen: absolutely, we'll share SOC2, ISO attestation, and a KMS integration guide after this call.
00:02:45 - Marisa Gomez: what's the delta in cost if we go 24 months vs 12?
00:02:50 - Laila Chen: we can do a committed discount at 24 months, roughly 12-18% off list depending on regions and burst capacity. i'll share a precise sheet.
00:03:03 - Ethan Park: also need to know SLA for latency p99 and how fallbacks work if a region is constrained — like do requests route to hosted US?
00:03:14 - Ravi Patel: routing is policy driven. you can prefer region, then fallback to next region or to a cheaper model variant. we'll show routing policy examples and a failover runbook.
00:03:28 - Tom Hsu: for the benchmarks, we care about p95 and p99 for sequence lengths 128 and 512, token throughput, and cold start behaviors. can you replicate prefix cache hits?
00:03:40 - Ravi Patel: yes — we'll run a dedicated cluster in eu-west with your traffic profile. we'll instrument KV cache hit rates to match your prefix distribution.
00:03:52 - Marisa Gomez: timeline on benchmarks?
00:03:55 - Laila Chen: ravi, what's realistic?
00:03:58 - Ravi Patel: i can spin up infra next week, run tests, and have results by Oct 28 if we get the traffic profile and creds.
00:04:07 - Marisa Gomez: okay that fits procurement schedule.
00:04:15 - Priya Singh: another compliance point — audit logs retention, RBAC, SSO/SAML integration, and encryption in transit and at rest. do you support customer audit log export to our Splunk?
00:04:26 - Ravi Patel: yes, audit logs can be exported in syslog/JSON to your ingestion. RBAC integrates with SSO/SAML and SCIM for user provisioning. we'll include templates.
00:04:38 - Ethan Park: there's also an internal proof-of-concept team that may want an on-prem package for some parts of the stack — what does that path look like?
00:04:48 - Laila Chen: Private deployment is available — control plane can be in your VPC, runtime can be on-prem. it's a longer engagement and typically for regulated workloads. we can discuss if the security gating asks push you that direction.
00:05:02 - Marisa Gomez: prefer hosted Dedicated if possible — less ops for us — but security needs to sign off.
00:05:10 - Laila Chen: totally — we'll push all security artifacts. procurement will want a clear SLA and termination clauses; legal is usually ok to align once security clears.
00:05:20 - Tom Hsu: small nit — in your earlier perf doc there's mention of quantization affecting quality. can we see quality regressions tests or evals?
00:05:29 - Ravi Patel: yes we'll attach eval sets and regen comparisons showing negligible quality changes for int8 profiles we recommend. we'll also run your prompt set as part of the benchmark.
00:05:42 - Ethan Park: good. on regions — ap-southeast needed for our Singapore customers; is that available and what's capacity lead time?
00:05:52 - Laila Chen: eu-west and ap-southeast are both available for Dedicated but capacity lead times vary by commit. with a 6-node reservation we can prioritize allocation — i'll confirm exact lead times in the pricing sheet.
00:06:07 - Marisa Gomez: can we get an option to burst into Hosted if Dedicated is saturated?
00:06:12 - Ravi Patel: yes, hybrid routing supports burst to Hosted tier with rules and cost controls. we'll show pricing for fallback.
00:06:23 - Priya Singh: encryption key ownership — if we use our KMS, can Redwood access keys?
00:06:29 - Ravi Patel: no, with customer-managed keys Redwood does not have plaintext access; integration is via envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys.
00:06:37 - Marisa Gomez: procurement will ask for change of control language and indemnity if we sign 24 months.
00:06:44 - Laila Chen: understood — we'll loop in legal on the next call.
00:06:49 - Ethan Park: status on current usage and cost — we saw costs jump and want optimization suggestions.
00:06:56 - Ravi Patel: we can propose batching, KV cache tuning, and model/quantization recommendations via Redwood Optimize. small changes can reduce per-token cost significantly. we'll include suggested config in the pricing packet.
00:07:10 - Tom Hsu: for the benchmark run, what metrics will you provide?
00:07:14 - Ravi Patel: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (RPS and tokens/s), GPU utilization, cache hit rate, and cost projection per 1M tokens.
00:07:24 - Marisa Gomez: perfect. procurement also wants start/end dates for a contract — do you support mid-month starts?
00:07:30 - Laila Chen: yes, start dates are flexible; we can prorate initial month.
00:07:36 - Ethan Park: last question — any red flags from our side to push to Private?
00:07:40 - Ravi Patel: only if you have strict data residency that requires all metadata control locally or want to avoid any managed control plane. otherwise Dedicated in-region usually satisfies most enterprise controls.
00:07:54 - Priya Singh: okay, i'll compile the final list of security asks and email it by Friday.
00:08:01 - Marisa Gomez: outreach — we'll review the pricing and try to decide by end of month.
00:08:06 - Laila Chen: recap of agreed items: we will send SOC2/ISO/KMS docs, Laila will share pricing, Ravi to run eu-west benchmark, Priya to send security checklist, tom to send traffic profile.
00:08:22 - Laila Chen: any other questions?
00:08:25 - Ethan Park: none from me.
00:08:27 - Tom Hsu: all good.
00:08:29 - Laila Chen: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and calendar invites.
00:08:35 - Marisa Gomez: appreciate it.

Notes on transcript quality: some words auto-transcribed incorrectly (eg. 'KV cache' sometimes as 'k v cash'), names occasionally bled together. Natural speech and interruptions preserved.
